item.title: Love and Deepspace Devs Issue Warning to Players After Deadly Drink Recipes Go Viral
item.description: The official social media account for the popular RPG-dating sim Love and Deepspace issued a warning to players after announcing some fictional cocktails with potentially disastrous real-world consequences if actually consumed.
item.content:encoded:
The official social media account for the popular RPG-dating sim Love and Deepspace issued a warning to players after announcing some fictional cocktails with potentially disastrous real-world consequences if actually consumed.

On September 28, Love and Deepspace revealed five ‘Shimmering Blend’ cocktail recipes as part of an in-game event, each themed around one of the game’s dashing romanceable characters. While they’re pretty to look at, you shouldn’t actually make some of these, as they include garnishes that are poisonous to humans.

For example, one of these drinks is made of pomegranate juice, with a garnish of cinnamon and datura. Another features sweet peach juice with a flame lily garnish and gelatin sheets.

There’s nothing wrong with peach and pomegranate juice, but these floral garnishes are making some players anxious that a fan might actually try to out the recipes themselves. Datura is a highly poisonous plant and is considered psychoactive; when consumed, it produces side effects like delirium, fever, tachychardia, and hallucinations.

Flame Lilies are also dangerous, as all parts of the plant contain a chemical called colchicine; while it’s used for medicinal purposes, it can be lethal, causing symptoms like fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and even hypovolemic shock, which causes the loss of lethal amounts of blood and bodily fluids.

It didn’t take long for concerned fans to point out these dangerous plants, fearing that some players might try their hand at making the cocktails for real. Commenters flooded the replies with calls for the Love and Deepspace account to delete the post completely, with one writing, “Delete this. This is literal poison. Nobody make this.”

Safety Notice: All drinks shown are fictional and for in-game purposes only. Do not attempt to recreate or consume them in reality.

— Love and Deepspace (@Love_Deepspace) September 30, 2026

“Hey, so some of these flowers are literally poisonous. Be careful. This is so reckless to post this,” another said.

"Don't try to recreate these drinks, they contain toxic plants!" yet another warned. "I can't believe this is posted as 'recipes.'"

Not long after, the LaDS account added a follow-up post with a safety notice, which reads: “All drinks shown are fictional and for in-game purposes only. Do not attempt to recreate or consume them in reality.”

In addition to calls from fans to delete the posts, the LaDS social media accounts continue to be flooded with photos of canceled love interest Valko, who was announced and subsequently canned before he was even released. This prompted an impressive movement from the game’s playerbase, who created shrines to the character and even gathered outside the developer’s physical offices to make their voices heard.

item.title: Former NFL Coach Mike Tomlin Is a Hardcore Minecraft Player, Reveals City He Took 12 Years to Build
item.description: Former NFL coach Mike Tomlin spent 19 seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers and won Super Bowl LXIII, and now he's added another major accomplishment to his resume: becoming a Minecraft YouTuber.
item.content:encoded:
Former NFL coach Mike Tomlin spent 19 seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers and won Super Bowl LXIII, and now he's added another major accomplishment to his resume: becoming a Minecraft YouTuber.

The former coach gave football fans a little something different when he launched his new YouTube channel earlier this week. With a profile picture taken in front of NBC's Football Night in America logo, watchers probably weren't expecting Tomlin's first upload to see him confess how his love for architecture and family led him to work on a Minecraft city he spent 12 years building.

"You know, 12 or 13 years ago, when my kids were in middle school, they'd be in their room all weekend and have friends over. They were obsessed with playing this game, Minecraft, that I knew nothing about," he explained as his son and channel operator, Dino, sat in the background. "I got interested because I just was mesmerized by what could occupy their attention for such large periods of time."

He admitted he lacked the "stick control" to handle something like Minecraft's Survival mode but still managed to find enjoyment in Creative Mode. That's where Mojang's systems really started to click.

"I like to build," he said. "I've always had an interest in architecture, and so forth, so I started doing this creative city. It was a means of spending time with them. They participated all over this city. All my kids have buildings."

However, as his kids went off to high school and college, their interest in Minecraft waned. For Tomlin, it was just beginning. In 2026, after 12 years of building, the sandbox phenomenon has become therapeutic for the former NFL coach, and what he's built has the internet in disbelief.

"This is where it all started for me," Tomlin said as a blocky blue pond surrounded by detailed city buildings faded into view. His tour then begins with a closer look at a hotel. This one building features a fully fleshed-out interior with labeled rooms, a lobby, a ballroom, a pool, bathrooms, and more. Tomlin even factored in how lighting might affect the views in some of these rooms – and that's just one of many locations he's made.

"I was always inspired," he added. "I'd go places, and I'd see things and buildings, and I get inspired, I go home, and I work on it."

Tomlin then referenced the off-campus housing around universities that he recreated after dropping Dino off at college. The color, floor plans, and other memorable elements all came from these memories, with much of his creation also built around different bodies of water.

Tomlin stepped down as the Steelers' coach in January 2026, with today's video showing how he's spent at least some of the downtime since. He spent years in the NFL, but it's his work as a Minecraft YouTuber that has everyone talking today.

— Barstool Sports (@barstoolsports) October 1, 2026

Aaron Rodgers: “CALL THE F*CKING PLAY!”

Mike McCarthy: “F*cking asshole”

*Loses to the Cleveland Browns*

Meanwhile, Mike Tomlin: pic.twitter.com/axnE3655rT

— NFL Memes (@NFLMemes) October 2, 2026

— Donny Football (@DonChed54) October 1, 2026

— ant ☘️ (@anthshiesty) October 1, 2026

"I'm obsessed why is he genuinely a better builder than me," content creator @Krtzyy said.

"Mike Tomlin becoming a Minecraft YouTuber was not on my bingo card for 2026," one X/Twitter user said.

Tomlin signed off, promising to take a closer look at his city in future videos. He also teased plans to show off something that "I think you're going to find interesting." Despite being maybe the most creative celebrity gamer to come out of 2026, the ex-NFL coach isn't the only notable name to share their love for gaming in the last year. Obsession breakout Inde Navarrette garnered attention for her The Last of Us and Call of Duty streams a few months ago. Newly announced X-Men star, Samara Weaving, is also a big gamer.

item.title: Disney Says Conversations About Buying Epic Games Are Not Happening 'Right Now'
item.description: Disney has responded after rumors suggested it was interested in buying Fortnite developer Epic Games.
item.content:encoded:
Disney has responded after rumors suggested it was interested in buying Fortnite developer Epic Games.

Disney president and chief creative officer Dana Walden touched on the company's relationship with Epic during an interview with Bloomberg Live. When asked if there have been talks about expanding their previously established relationship with a full-on acquisition, she said that strategy isn't something Disney is entertaining, at least right now.

"Well, I think that it was pretty obvious that we had very serious conversations about an investment and an equity stake," Walden responded. "Those are not the conversations we're having right now, but we have a great partnership and a number of launches coming up over the next two years that are going to demonstrate the value of this partnership."

The relationship referenced here was solidified when Disney announced it acquired a $1.5 billion stake in Epic back in early 2024. It was a massive play that it promised would result in collaborations across Fortnite and more in the future.

"Our exciting new relationship with Epic Games will bring together Disney’s beloved brands and franchises with the hugely popular Fortnite in a transformational new games and entertainment universe," then-CEO Bob Iger said. "This marks Disney’s biggest entry ever into the world of games and offers significant opportunities for growth and expansion. We can’t wait for fans to experience the Disney stories and worlds they love in groundbreaking new ways."

We're still feeling the shockwaves of that deal, but some suspected it could evolve into more than a simple partnership. Tech reporter Alex Heath said in March 2026 that some Disney executives were "waiting for that moment" to go all in on an acquisition. Then, in April, Bloomberg reported that Epic was working on an extraction shooter featuring Disney characters with plans to launch in November 2026.

We're now kicking off October with no official mention of that unannounced project, but that doesn't mean Disney x Epic is going anywhere any time soon. While an acquisition isn't in the cards, Walden's promise regarding "a number of launches" set to arrive in the next few years suggests there is plenty more to talk about.

We'll have to wait and see how the two entertainment giants work together moving forward. In the meantime, you can read some of the other ways Disney and Epic have bolstered their relationship, including a Disneyland-exclusive Fortnite skin and officially licensed Star Wars minigames.

item.title: Vibe-Coded Mashup Mods Have Taken Over X This Week
item.description: I have spent the last three days scrolling through some of the most insane mod videos I've ever seen. Modders are taking games that have been decompiled with Claude, and mashing them up with other games. As the week has gone on, there have only been more clips of these mods pouring out on X/Twitter.
item.content:encoded:
I have spent the last three days scrolling through some of the most insane mod videos I've ever seen. Modders are taking games that have been decompiled with Claude, and mashing them up with other games. As the week has gone on, there have only been more clips of these mods pouring out on X/Twitter.

One person created a mashup of World of Warcraft and Call of Duty: World at War; another combined Escape From Tarkov with Skyrim. There’s even one that takes Insomniac’s Spider-Man and combines it with Batman Arkham City, where the player is able to swing around Batman’s turf.

These mods are everywhere online right now, though they thankfully haven’t filtered into modding websites like Nexus Mods yet. But, with the sheer volume of these mods and with how accessible Opus 5.5 is, it feels like it’s only a matter of time before the gates are fully torn down. And if that happens, it could change the face of the modding scene entirely.

Why Now?

Claude Opus 5.5 launched last week, promising cheaper tokens and more efficient code work. I'm sure that Anthropic meant for it to be used by professionals, but gamers have used it to create some of the weirdest mods I have ever seen.

Opus is a model that can power AI agents, which can be deployed to create entire games from the engine, to the art and enemy behavior. Brendan Jowett has a great video on YouTube of the model in action: He develops little slices of video games and compares them directly with the same tasks from OpenAI’s Astra 6 model. While the results of both are far from what you’d expect from a fully featured game, Claude’s new model has clearly come a long way.

The problem with the examples in Jowett’s video is that while the models are good at piecing together disparate parts of a game, enemy AI (lol) and art assets are lackluster to say the least. In one of the slices, a space combat sim, the space fighter flys at a diagonal angle, while moving in a straight line ahead, and shooting. In another slice enemies completely ignore the player character.

As good as Claude Opus 5.5 seems to be, it’s still lightyears away from developing something like a true mashup of Minecraft and Elden Ring from scratch. But the model doesn’t have to start from scratch.

The big, driving force behind a lot of these mods is decompilation, where people are pointing Opus at a game and letting the agent break it down to its source code (here’s a handy blog if you want to really get in the weeds). Just earlier today, we covered Halo: Combat Evolved being decompiled and ported to run natively in a browser. Once that step is complete, it takes little effort to take that source code and work huge swaths of games into other games as mods, and with very little input from the user.

Couple that with the relatively affordable tokens, and it shouldn’t be surprising that X/Twitter’s generally pro-AI users went wild with it, creating hundreds of mashups. And it doesn’t seem like it’s slowing down any time soon; what started off as a weird video that my boss sent me on Tuesday has now evolved to the point where I can’t even open X/Twitter without seeing a deluge of these mods.

Piracy?

The obvious problem with all of this is that these models are breaking open games developed by real people, getting the source code and then just mashing stuff together without consideration or permission from the original developers. That’s nothing particularly new – the modding scene is definitely no stranger to mashups, all the Thomas the Tank Engine mods are proof of that. However, this trend might be breaking into new territory, thanks to decompilation.

This could be another reason none of these mods have made their way onto any distribution platforms. Nexus Mods doesn’t outright ban AI-generated content, but it doesn’t let people use AI tools to upload content that they don’t have the rights to.

In a blog post from 2023, Nexus laid out its rules around AI generated content. The policy states that, “In order to prevent any issues with your mods, we encourage you to avoid using these tools unless you have explicit permission to use all the assets. This is particularly true for AI-generated voice acting but also covers images, models, code and anything else that you can use this technology to create.”

Every single one of these passthrough mods are using images, models, and code that the people generating them don’t have the rights to. But it’s only a matter of time until some platform holder allows these mods to be hosted, and I’m sure a massive legal battle will happen immediately afterwards.

The Modding Community Hates This

Way before all of these Claude-authored mod videos started cropping up online, people had been creating mods by hand for years, typically out of pure love for the game. It shouldn’t be surprising, then, that a lot of mod authors aren’t fans of this phenomenon.

Mod authors have been expressing their frustration on X/Twitter as this has been happening. “I mod games and I'm not shy about the fact that I use AI to do it. I hate this bullshit ‘trend’. Pure slop, there's nothing creative about this at all,” kran27_ posted. “AI has a lot of potential in the modding scene, but the shit that's getting the clicks is this jingling keys bullshit.”

Kran wasn’t alone, with discountmodder ready to just leave the scene, saying, “Dude I'm really disappointed. If this becomes the permanent state of modding, this may be my last project. I don't wanna be involved in an AI slop-factory.”

I can’t escape the feeling that most of these mashups are born from people just playing with a new AI model and seeing what will happen, and I hope that this weird trend will die off soon. Modding is one of the best parts of PC gaming, and there is a lot of incredible content that people make just because they love a game. Some of the best games started off as mods, after all, and without them we never would have got the likes of Half-Life or League of Legends.

I hope that this is just a trend, rather than a sign of where the modding scene is heading. Fortunately, because these mods seemingly only exist to farm engagement on Twitter (at least so far), you don’t have to worry too much about them if you just want to start a new modded run of The Witcher 3 Remastered. If anything, it just means that if you want to avoid AI content, you need to pay even more attention to who you’re getting your mods from.

item.title: Ex-Rockstar Boss Dan Houser Doesn't Play a Lot of Open-World Games – and Doesn't Plan to Play GTA 6
item.description: Dan Houser, the former co-boss of Rockstar Games and former creative director on the Grand Theft Auto series, doesn't play a lot of open-world games. And he doesn't plan on playing GTA 6 either. But it's for a good creative reason: he doesn't want to be influenced by them as he works on his two new game projects at his new enterprise, Absurd Ventures.
item.content:encoded:
Dan Houser, the former co-boss of Rockstar Games and former creative director on the Grand Theft Auto series, doesn't play a lot of open-world games. And he doesn't plan on playing GTA 6 either. But it's for a good creative reason: he doesn't want to be influenced by them as he works on his two new game projects at his new enterprise, Absurd Ventures.

"Given that I spend a large amount of time trying to make open-world games, and the rest of my conscious time trying to figure out innovative ways to market them, I don’t need to see what other people are [doing]," he told Variety. I’m always trying to think about new ways of doing it, not sit there in some kind of comparison of what I would have done differently."

"It’s not my job within any company that I’ve ever worked at, thankfully, to be the person that understands what everyone else is doing," Houser continued. "I’m trying to think about new ways of doing it. So when we worked on Red Dead Redemption, as soon as we started working, I never watched another Western. I never watched The Sopranos until after I left Rockstar. I saw one episode, because my girlfriend-now-wife and I did watch the finale in real time. I’d not seen any of it before that moment. And then I watched it all during COVID. And I’m grateful. It’s so good that it would have disrupted everything I did on GTA, had I watched at the time. So I really try and avoid things that I think are going to overly influence me."

"I really try and avoid things that I think are going to overly influence me."

On not playing many other open-world games, Houser said, "I find when I play them, I can almost deconstruct the strengths and weaknesses of the team in real time and it’s distracting. I’m always thinking, ‘Well, their animation team is weak, but I think this game design is fantastic.’ And, ‘Oh, I can imagine that meeting when they discuss this feature.’ I’m not a game designer, I’m a sort of creative director. So I’m trying to always find new things that haven’t been done before, or that I can steal from older media, quite frankly or just inspired me or things I always thought about."

Houser's new company, Absurd Ventures, is currently working on two games, as discussed in my all-too-brief conversation with him at LA Comic-Con last year. The studio has already released American Caper, a graphic novel series. Its double-sized season-finale issue drops next month – a week before GTA 6 – along with the book "A Better Paradise."

item.description: Find out where to preorder Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution—Delta Reign at MSRP in the US and UK before Elite Trainer Boxes and Booster Displays sell out.
item.content:encoded:
The upcoming Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution—Delta Reign expansion officially launches on November 6, 2026. It's the last announced Pokémon TCG set for 2026, continuing Pokémon TCG’s spotlight on Mega Evolution Pokémon with the return of Mega Rayquaza, last seen in Ancient Origins in 2015.

For reference, here’s a quick overview of what’s available in the Delta Reign lineup.

A collector favourite, the ETB includes 9 booster packs, exclusive promo cards, card sleeves, energy cards, and game accessories.

The classic booster box comes with 36 booster packs. This is the best option if you want to maximise your chances of opening all the set's chase cards or do large pack openings.

Last, but by no means least, Booster Bundles include six booster packs from the Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution—Delta Reign expansion, each with 10 cards, 1 Basic Energy, and 1 Pokémon TCG Live code card.

Initial pre-orders went live on the Pokémon Center at the end of September, and it was a bloodbath. Queues were 12 hours long, and fans reported numerous tech issues.

Oh well that Pokemon Center drop was a shit show, tons of errors and selling out that quick with reduced limits? Normally even when ETB's sell out Booster Boxes and Bundles last for a couple more hours but not this time.

It just screams that this set is underprinted, maybe…

— Pokemon UK PBST - Restock Alerts & News (@PBSTUK) September 30, 2026

​If you want to get your hands on this set, you’ll need to be quick. Here are the best places to check out if you want to secure any of the products.

We’ll be regularly updating this page with confirmed deals, so bookmark this page, keep checking back in, and follow @IGNFinds on Twitter/X for the latest updates.

Where to Preorder Delta Reign at MSRP

Your best bet to buy Delta Reign at MSRP is the Pokémon Center UK and US. MSRP for Delta Reign is $59/£56.99 for the Elite Trainer Box (ETB).

The first wave has been, but it’s likely that there will be more soon. Keep an eye on this page for more information.

At the Pokemon Center, you can also pick up the exclusive Elite Trainer Box, which features extra promo items and metallic coins/dice not found in standard retail ETBs. For this expansion, you'll get 1 full-art foil promo card featuring Kyogre with a Pokémon Center logo.

You can also try your luck at securing the booster and display boxes - these usually stick around a bit longer than an ETB. Unfortunately, right now - these are also all sold out!

​If you don’t manage to get lucky at the standard retail offerings, you can always check out TCGplayer - a third party reseller that will offer preorders. Unfortunately, you’re likely to pay extra here due to the third party sellers looking to capitalize. In saying that, if you’re desperate to get some pulls, or lock in your booster boxes, case pre-orders, and bundle deals, this is run by hobbyists who usually put up pre-orders early. Just bear in mind it’s not 100% guaranteed if you order from here.

For the 30th Celebration set, Amazon UK and US did a lottery system where you had to sign up for the MSRP. This helped with queues and demand. It’s unclear right now whether they’ll repeat this for Delta Reign. Currently, there are no listings. As one of the biggest retailers out there, Amazon usually gets a good amount of stock, so keep an eye out for these!

Where to Preorder in the US

Best Buy

Best Buy is a pretty good shout when it comes to Pokémon TCG orders. To boost your chances, look into My Best Buy Plus - a membership program that costs $29.99 per year. You can get members-only prices on certain products, an extended return window, free expedited shipping. and exclusive early access to TCG pre-orders.

Walmart

Walmart is known for videos showing people scrambling for the last ETB on the shelves, but you can skip the launch-day chaos by pre-ordering online. You could sign up for Walmart+ for $98 a year or $12.95 a month. This membership gives you free delivery from stores on orders over $35, gas discounts of 10 cents per gallon, and access to Paramount+ or Peacock streaming. That’s a pretty good deal!

Where to Preorder in the UK

Magic Madhouse

Magic Madhouse is a really good choice for UK Trainers, especially if you’re hunting down singles. Currently, there’s no listing yet, but with the Pokémon Center pre-orders dropping, they’re only usually a few weeks behind.

Smyths Toys

If you prefer buying in-store, Smyths Toys is a great option. There is an online option too, but they usually sell out quikc. Check your local stores availability online to see what’s in stock!

Just bring some protective gear if you go to an in-person launch event, just in case. I’m joking. Kinda.

Argos

Argos is a bit of a Calyrex (dark horse, hah) when it comes to stocking Pokémon cards. They’re not the most reliable, but they do occasionally have stock.

What’s in the Delta Reign Lineup?

Unlike the 30th Celebration, which was the first-ever simultaneous global release, Delta Reign is out now in Japan, known as Storm Esmerelda. Unsurprisingly, the biggest chase card is the star of the show, the Mega Rayquaza ex Mega Ultra Rare. Illustrated by takuyoa, this card reached an all-time high on TCGPlayer of $2,166.69.

But there’s loads of gorgeous chase cards in here. If there’s a single you’re after in particular, it might be worth checking out places like TCGPlayer to save some money in the long run.

I imagine, with the popularity of Mega Rayquaza, Delta Reign might be a mad rush for stock. Fingers crossed the prices stay low!

item.title: GTA 6 Age Rating Confirms New Details on Sex, Drug Use, Decapitation, and More
item.description: GTA 6 has received a rating of PEGI 18, revealing mentions of "decapitation," the ability for players to snort cocaine at any time, "scenes of sexual fetishes," and much more.
item.content:encoded:
UPDATE October 2, 2026, 11:39 a.m. PT: PEGI has seemingly updated its website to remove the age rating for GTA 6.

The PEGI 18 page – which, as viewed by IGN, included what appeared to be new details about GTA 6 – is no longer available. In its place is a blank listing that says, "The requested page could not be found." Users on X/Twitter have captured and shared an image of the listing and have continued to share its contents across social media. IGN has reached out to PEGI for comment.

Grand Theft Auto VI PEGI rating is now up!https://t.co/av3HXd6GQf pic.twitter.com/6MhVcAA1xc

— iGrandTheftAuto.com (@iGrandTheftAuto) October 2, 2026

ORIGINAL STORY: GTA 6 has received an age rating of PEGI 18, revealing mentions of "decapitation," the ability for players to snort cocaine at any time, "scenes of sexual fetishes," and much more.

The update, which can be found on the Pan European Game Information board's website, gives players a relatively in-depth description of Rockstar Games' megaton video game ahead of its launch in November. The PEGI 18 rating arrives just one day after GTA 6 received its official ESRB rating, which, also unsurprisingly, resulted in an "M for Mature."

GTA 6's rating describes a story that allows players to take control of "Jason Duval or Lucia Caminos, two criminals who become involved in a criminal conspiracy following a failed robbery." It adds that they'll work together as "they become increasingly entangled in criminal activities" in Vice City, with gameplay that, as we've already seen, is par for the course when it comes to Grand Theft Auto.

What's different about GTA 6 is the unprecedented detail Rockstar has shoved into the game, with previous footage showing off an open-world sandbox with enough activities to make up for the 13-year wait. PEGI dived into that, too, but there are still even more new highlights to go over.

The board described the game's violence as "bloody with a high degree of realism." Some weapons will be more brutal than others, with some said to be "able to cause greater damage, such as detailed decapitation and dismemberment." This time around, Rockstar has made drug use "frequent and prominent," with players able to partake in illicit substances. Cocaine is said to be especially important in Vice City, with the rating promising that Jason and Lucia will be able to use the substance directly from their inventory, as it can be "snorted directly from their hand at any time."

The GTA 6 PEGI description also touched on "strong sexual themes," which include "nudity, scenes of intercourse, and occasional scenes of sexual fetishes." It's a lot that we knew and some details that we didn't, but you can read the "content specific issues" section of the summary in its entirety below.

"This game contains frequent depictions of violence; due to the free roam nature of the game the player can harm all other characters inhabiting the environment," PEGI said. "This includes civilians, criminals and the authorities. Violence is bloody with a high degree of realism, with certain weapons being able to cause greater damage such as detailed decapitation and dismemberment.

"Drug use is frequent and prominent with the player being able to partake in drug use with others and to use illegal drugs directly from their inventory. Most notably, cocaine can be carried around by the player and snorted directly from their hand at any time.

"There are also strong sexual themes, including nudity, scenes of intercourse and occasional scenes of sexual fetishes. In various night clubs the player can also pay for private dances, during which, the game allows the player to move their hands onto the dancers’ breasts and buttocks."

The PEGI age rating also mentioned "other issues," including that domestic animals can be harmed, though not in the same detail as humans. The word "f**k" is also featured prominently in the game, while the word "c**t" is only occasionally featured. The description also said that "discriminatory language can be heard in the TV shows and on the radio channels."

Finally, GTA 6 reminds players that they will have the option to purchase in-game items, though it's still unclear what this entails. In August, it was reported that Rockstar would not include microtransactions or generative AI in the game.

GTA 6 is still on course to launch for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19, 2026. You can read more about how Rockstar has ramped up its marketing tactics here, and you can see what we learned from some new screenshots here. While we wait for any more updates, you can read IGN's interview and preview.

item.title: 4 Things to Focus on Outside Combat in Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave
item.content:encoded:
We’re back for a new installment in our The Long Game series, where we break down things you can invest in early in games that will pay off long-term. Today we’re focusing on Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave, the huge new installment in the long-running series that takes you to the capital of the Dagdan Empire to be a gladiator in the Heroic Games.

Like its predecessor Three Houses, Fortune’s Weave has a split narrative with multiple protagonists. However, this time around, you don’t have to choose one route. You can follow the stories of Cai, Leda, Dietrich, and Theodora in any order and can switch between them at any time once you reach Dagsion, the central hub city.

As with the rest of the Fire Emblem series, Fortune’s Weave is centered on grid-based strategy combat. But it also features a heavy focus on activities outside of combat, with access to a world map you can traverse between story battles. You can find dungeons, towns, traveling merchants, and skirmishes with roving enemies.

That’s on top of running around the giant city of Dagsion, which is full of shops, activities, and people to meet. It can all be a little overwhelming, especially if you’re new to the series and aren’t sure where to start. So that’s what we’re here to help with. Here are four things outside of combat that you can (and should) start taking advantage of as soon as you can.

Show Your Support

Support levels and conversations have long been a staple of the Fire Emblem series, with characters amassing points whenever they fight next to each other or provide healing or support in combat. Fortune’s Weave expands that system and adds new ways to build support outside of combat, which you should take advantage of whenever possible.

The primary way of building support is by eating meals together at the inn, which will be available to all protagonists very early in the game. Three people can eat together at once, and everyone has their own food preferences. The inn menu changes daily, and when you pick your group of three, you can see how they feel about each meal.

The amount of support points everyone gains is based on how much they like the meal, so don’t try to force people to eat stuff they don’t like. Meals are particularly helpful for building support points with people who aren’t actively in your party and are a vital way to convince recruits to join you (more on that in a bit), since you can’t build support with them in combat.

You’ll eventually unlock arena training, where you can assign two fighters to train with each other in a variety of ways. This will boost both fighters’ command of weapons, magic, or movement types, while also giving them support points with each other. Arena training is the most valuable way to prepare characters for more advanced combat classes. Plus, it’s available every week, so don’t forget to come back to Dagsion every once in a while to take advantage of it.

Raise Your Renown

Each protagonist will learn about Renown once they get to Dagsion early in the game, and it’s basically a stat that measures how well known you are in the city. Increasing your Renown adds important boosts at certain thresholds, will make it possible to recruit more characters, and it’s a big part of the central gameplay loop of Fortune’s Weave.

All protagonists can take on subquests given out by people throughout Dagsion, most of which will take you onto the world map to find items or get rid of certain enemies. These subquests each give Renown and all have deadlines, but they’re usually pretty forgiving, so you should have plenty of time to do them all.

Paralogues are the exception to that standard. These are more significant side quests that expand on the stories of individual characters. Fire Emblem veterans will already be familiar with paralogues, but they're handled differently in Fortune's Weave than the rest of the series. You can only start one if you talk to the right character in Dagsion during a set period of time, and the deadlines for paralogues are strict (in the most extreme case, there's one on Dietrich's path you can only get on one specific date).

This can be an issue because you might spend an extended period on the world map and blow right past the cutoff date without even realizing a paralogue was available. You won't receive any in-game notification, you just have to be in Dagsion on the correct dates. Completing a paralogue nets you 20,000 gold, a bunch of Renown, and unlocks recruitment for certain characters, so they're very worthwhile. I don't normally recommend playing with a guide, but this is one area where I think it's a good idea to look up the information beforehand. You need to be aware of the dates when paralogues are available so you can plan accordingly. Luckily, IGN has a full breakdown of their dates across all protagonists.

You can also earn Renown by visiting gods in their temples in Dagsion. This becomes available early in the game, but it can be easy to forget about since you don’t get reminded about it. On the map, there are icons for each god’s temple. You might notice that on some days, one of those icons is yellow, which means that god is there in person and available to visit. If you continue chatting with the same god, they’ll get chummy with you and might reveal some additional information about themselves or lore about the world.

While completing subquests and paralogues is the base way everyone can gain Renown, each protagonist also has an additional one that’s unique to them. Cai’s involves doing more quests, called kindness quests. Dietrich can summon enemies to battle at any time, as well as duel combatants in dungeons to steal their combat arts. Theodora gets resource requests that allow her to trade items you’ve gathered for Renown. And for Leda, remember to check the tavern in Dagsion at the start of each chapter. She’ll have new performance requests in certain cities on the world map, where she can dance to receive thousands of gold and hundreds of Renown at once.

Mind Your Materials

Character levels and class progression are obviously important in Fortune’s Weave, but don’t forget about their equipment. You’ll start with wooden weapons, but the armory will quickly add bronze and iron versions that are significantly more powerful. You should upgrade as soon as you’re able to.

In Chapter 6, regardless of whose path you’re following, you’ll be introduced to the blacksmith. The main one is in Dagsion, but some bigger towns on the world map will have one too. They allow you to spend money and smithing materials to upgrade your weapons, with basic weapons only requiring Smithing Stones and more specialized equipment requiring unique materials.

You can gather these materials on the world map, but the best places to find them are mines. These dungeons have crystal deposits you can smash that will earn you guaranteed smithing materials. As you’d expect, higher level mines will have more unique materials, and you can gather a bunch of them in one trip.

Dungeons will also be filled with boxes and barrels you can smash with an attack, and ones that hold items will have golden sparkles on them. You can get a variety of materials this way, including stones and food.

Food can be used at rest spots in dungeons or feast spots on the world map to restore your health and magic, which is particularly important when you’re planning on staying outside of town for a while. Some quests and recruits will also require particular vegetables, meat, or fish, so try to keep a variety of food items on hand in case you need them.

If you’re playing as Cai, he can also use food as bait to lure out animals to catch and use as mounts. If you use rare food, noted by a blue icon with a sparkle in the corner, you’re more likely to attract rare animals. Just make sure you use the kind of food each animal likes: orniuses like fish, horses and pegasi prefer vegetables, while wild bau like meat.

Rally Your Recruits

No matter which protagonist you’re leading, your core group of characters won’t be enough to take on later chapters. You’ll need to add to your ranks by recruiting some of the many characters scattered around Dagsion, but you don’t have to wander aimlessly and hope you run into them. All characters will be noted by dots on the map: an orange dot marks a character you haven’t met yet, a green dot means you’ve spoken to them but haven’t recruited them, and a blue dot means they’re a member of your party. Once you’ve met them, you can also teleport to them directly by selecting them on the third tab of the map.

Recruitment combines much of what we’ve already talked about in this article. All characters require that you have specific support and Renown levels, which you can see when you select them on the map or by clicking the “Character Info” option when you talk to them. Some recruits will also have additional requirements, like paying them money, retrieving a particular item, or completing a paralogue, side quest, or story chapter.

In order to recruit anyone, you first need to give them a gift. Any gift will do for the first one, but after that, you should try to find ones you think they’ll like based on their personal preferences. Doing this will also make it possible to dine with them at the inn, which is how you’ll raise their support level high enough to recruit them. The only support level that matters is the one they have with your current protagonist, so make sure you’re inviting both characters to meals.

Recruits have different requirements for each of the protagonists. Someone who needs 10 Renown to be recruited by Cai might only need 4 Renown to be recruited by Dietrich. Meals and gifts are limited each week, so you don’t want to spread yourself too thin by trying to appeal to too many recruits at once. It’s wise to focus on a select few recruits at a time, then move on to new ones once you’re successful.

New recruitable characters will continually be added as each storyline progresses, including the leaders of squads you defeat during the Heroic Games. So keep an eye on the map in each chapter to see if there are any new orange dots. And just in case this is the kind of thing you worry about: Recruiting a character with one protagonist will not remove them from the pool for other protagonists. So you don’t have to be concerned about leaving later protagonists with nobody to recruit.

There you have it, four things to make sure you get a handle on early in Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave. For more coverage of this massive game, check out our review, recruitment guide, and 18 things the game doesn’t tell you.

item.title: MTG’s Hobbit Cards Are the Closest Thing to Owning Rare Tolkien Memorabilia, and Perfect for Collectors
item.description: Here's why Magic: The Gathering’s small-ish Hobbit set somehow surpasses the massive Lord of the Rings crossover for die-hard Tolkien collectors, just one month after its release.
item.content:encoded:
For the second time, and likely the last, Magic: The Gathering has taken players back to Middle-Earth with its The Hobbit set (its fifth of the year, if you can believe it), and it’s been pretty great.

That’s perhaps to be expected since the original book laid out a lot of what we consider fantasy tropes. Dragons, goblins, dwarves, and more are represented here in a smaller set than the Lord of the Rings one, all of which have gone on to inspire Magic cards in their own right.

Still, given how tricky it can be to get some products, there’s a good chance that finding Hobbit items can feel like searching for the Arkenstone in Smaug’s treasure hoard. And yet, it feels like, in a way, that’s kind of the point.

Tolkien Collectors Will Love The Hobbit Set

J.R.R. Tolkien’s influence on the world of fantasy cannot be overstated, and there’s a reason that so many early editions of his works have fetched colossal sums of money.

As an example, back in 2025, a fully signed Lord of the Rings first-edition set sold for around £287,700 (or $337,000). That marks the high point of spending, but it’s not an outlier by any stretch.

An unsigned first edition of the book also sold in 2025 for $250,000, while a collection of manuscripts from the author that includes notes written in Elvish has sold for over $200,000, too.

Naturally, memorabilia sells big, too, notably from Peter Jackson’s iconic movies. Props, costumes, and limited-edition art prints fetch piles of gold to make a covetous dragon blush, and that includes pieces from The Hobbit movies, too.

Of course, those figures are colossal compared to the price of even the most expensive cards in The Hobbit set, but there’s crossover there, too.

Whereas the Lord of the Rings set offered full art cards with a slick border treatment that highlighted the series’ characters across heroes and villains, The Hobbit leans into the series’ literary origins with book cover-inspired designs that carry a “well-read” look that makes them feel unique amongst Magic’s wide-ranging treatment offerings.

This writer was lucky enough to pack Gandalf, Goblins’ Bane and Smaug, Wicked Worm in the treatment, and they’ve almost instantly become two of my favorite Magic cards I own. There’s just something about the way they look textured that makes them feel like the latest in a long line of Tolkien memorabilia.

In fact, I’d go so far as to say that these are my favorite treatments we’ve received in years - and an ideal inclusion for any serious collector.

That doesn’t make it any easier to find the cards, mind…

item.title: Brand New GTA 6 Screenshots Focus on Lucia and Jason's Relationship
item.description: Rockstar has further ramped up its GTA 6 marketing today with the launch of several new screenshots focusing on protagonists Lucia and Jason.
item.content:encoded:
Rockstar has further ramped up its GTA 6 marketing today with the launch of several new screenshots focusing on protagonists Lucia and Jason.

GTA 6's dynamic criminal duo can be seen in four new images published via Love Magazine, which features an illustration of the couple on its cover, and a black-and-white screenshot of the pair in more casual clothes (Jason in a white vest, jacked arms on show, Lucia in a leopard-print crop top).

Two more images show Lucia and Jason together in the booth of a diner, but sat opposite. Is this the setting of a heist planning session, or are the two about to hold-up the very diner they're sat in? Are they having a date, or an argument about the way their criminal undertakings are going? What looks like a large bag set to be filled with stolen money suggests something is afoot.

Next up are images of Lucia and Jason in more stylish clothes (well, Jason is in bike leathers), and looking fierce while playing pool in what appears to be a biker bar.

The article also includes further detail from Rockstar senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, who discussed the pair's pursuit of the American Dream. GTA 6 portrays this as the couple seeking the ability to own a house and pay off their various debts, rather than a desire to become billionaires. “If you are going to put all this effort into creating a version of today’s world, it has to be more over the top, more insane, more in your face,” Humphries said. “Otherwise, you could just go outside and live in the real world.”

"We wanted both protagonists to be vulnerable, tough, flawed, right sometimes, wrong sometimes, able to learn from each other,” game writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern told Love. “That’s what we felt made them authentic, and a great team.” Game writer Alexa D’Agostino added: “When you are focusing on writing a fully realised person with their own wants, you’re going to get something perfectly imperfect — with clichés, but also undeniably real.”

Speaking of GTA 6 marketing ramping up, The Miami Heat announced it would be heading to Vice City for its next NBA match against the Milwaukee Bucks. The one-night-only event, hosted live on ESPN, has been dubbed A Night in Vice City, and will see the home team donning an "all-new uniform on a never-before-seen court."

item.title: Pokémon TCG Reportedly Launching First-Ever Valentine’s Day Set in 2027
item.description: Pokémon TCG is reportedly launching its first-ever Valentine's Day box set on January 27, 2027, featuring mini packs and packaging that folds into a classroom mailbox.
item.content:encoded:
The Pokémon Company is intending to launch the franchise's very first dedicated Valentine's Day collection on January 27, 2027, according to a recent report from Pokébeach.

While the Valentine set is yet to be officially confirmed, the leaks reportedly suggest that the "Pokémon TCG Valentine’s Box" will be similar in practice to the popular Trick or Trade Halloween series, rather than a full expansion release like Pokémon TCG's Delta Reign or Chaos Rising expansions.

These seasonal sets typically come in compact foil packs containing three cards, alongside sticker sheets. The Halloween releases were given their own pumpkin-stamped Pikachu, so I'd put good money on the Valentine's version getting some kind of suitably pink Pika stamp.

The Trick or Trade range was originally designed as a way for kids to hand out Pokémon cards while trick-or-treating, effectively giving them a Pokémon-themed alternative to candy. Given how expensive some Halloween sweets have become, perhaps the cards aren't such a bad substitute.

The reported Valentine's Box appears to be taking a similar approach, with the packaging and packs seemingly designed around giving cards to friends or handing them out in the classroom. The box is also apparently designed to fold into a little cardboard mailbox, allowing cards to be handed out to classmates in the same way kids might exchange Valentine's cards at school.

That's a cute idea, although given the current state of the Pokémon TCG market, I'm not entirely convinced every box will make it into the hands of an actual child.

Previous seasonal releases have generally focused on reprinted cards rather than introducing a bunch of new full-art cards, but that hasn't stopped sealed products from holding surprisingly strong secondary-market value. The Trick or Trade BOOster Bundle (last seen in 2025), for example, contains 40 mini packs with three cards apiece, and currently has a market value of around $75.99 at TCGplayer.

That makes the potential Valentine's release one to keep an eye on, particularly if it proves to be another limited seasonal product. Previous holiday releases have sold out well ahead of launch, so the real competition could come when preorders eventually open.

There's also currently no word on which Pokémon will take centre stage in the mini set. My vote would be Enamorus, although Fairy-type Pokémon aren't currently part of the TCG's standard format... Yet.

I’d also love to see Sylveon - its pink color scheme and cute ribbons would be perfect. Plus, it evolves by friendship! Other options could be Audino and Blissey, since both are linked with care and kindness - qualities that suit Valentine's Day well- or even Pikachu in loveheart-themed clothing might also show up.

Sylveon would also be an obvious choice. Its pink colour scheme and ribbons are practically made for Valentine's Day, while the fact that it evolves through friendship feels particularly appropriate. Audino and Blissey could also fit the theme nicely given their associations with care and kindness, while a loveheart-themed Pikachu would hardly come as a surprise.

item.title: Blizzard Adds Beloved 'Kyle's Gone Missing' Quest to World of Warcraft: Forever
item.description: For as much as World of Warcraft Forever has been making an effort to preserve the vanilla WoW experience, there are just some things in the game's history that must be added, and the quest 'Kyle's Gone Missing!' is one of them. And Blizzard just added it to Forever.
item.content:encoded:
For as much as World of Warcraft Forever has been making an effort to preserve the vanilla WoW experience, there are just some things in the game's history that must be added, and the quest 'Kyle's Gone Missing!' is one of them. And Blizzard just added it to Forever.

'Kyle's Gone Missing!' was added during the Burning Crusade expansion through a Make-a-Wish campaign in 2007 for Ezra Chatterton, who was diagnosed with brain cancer earlier that year. Chatterton, who went by the in-game name of Ephoenix, voiced the quest-giver, Ahab Wheathoof, and had his dog Kyle added to the game, which players were then tasked with finding. The quest went live in patch 2.1.2 on June 19, 2007, and has been in the game ever since.

Sadly, a little over a year later, in October 2008, Chatterton passed away at the age of 12. The quest has remained a beloved part of the game ever since, and Chatterton has also been referenced multiple times, with Blizzard re-naming the Elder of Thunderbluff (who shows up during the annual Lunar Festival) after him in Wrath of the Lich King.

But because the quest was added during The Burning Crusade, it's not part of the original game, which meant it wouldn't be in World of Warcraft Forever – even if the zone where the quest takes place is the Tauren starting zone. But, after players asked Blizzard to bring the quest to Forever, it's officially been added.

Blizzard added the patch after players asked for it in the forums, when user Nyaria posted saying, "My Husband was very sad that the Make a Wish Quest involving Kyle wasn’t in Mulgore." They even acknowledged that it doesn't fit the 'Vanilla-only' ethos, but stood by it, saying, "Yes it wasn’t added until TBC, but this is WoW: Forever, we already have new quests added in, and it was a cute little quest, and a Make a Wish addition for a poor kid."

Luckily, shortly after that thread was posted Blizzard community manager Kaivax simply posted: "We're working on it. Stay tuned." The entire rest of the thread is full of players thanking Kaivax and the rest of the Forever team for adding the quest. One player, Ikory, claimed to have been a Make-a-Wish kid who survived and thanked Blizzard in a long post, which they signed off with: "I spent 30 years in crippling pain, with a failing heart, that had to be repaired every few years. I am a survivor. I was that kid who was supposed to die. Now I have a freaken PhD. I lived. Make-A-Wish helped me have hope as a kid. I got my wish. I’m glad Ezra got his wish. Thank you Blizzard for still caring about us Make-A-Wish kids after all these years."

Now, just four days later, the quest is officially live in the World of Warcraft beta, as a part of the October 1 patch.

Johnny Cash, the Blizzard Principal Designer who added the quest, posted on X/Twitter, saying "I had the honor and privilege of bringing "Kyle's Gone Missing!" into WoW: Forever. Ezra Chatterton was an enormous WoW fan, the creator and voice actor behind Ahab Wheathoof, and the creator of Kyle. A tear was shed during this one, my friends. Rest in peace, Ezra."

The quest isn't hard to get to, especially if you start off as a Tauren. Ezra's NPC is in Bloodhoof Village, which is the first town you get to while questing in Mulgore. You can pick up the quest as soon as you hit level 5, and you'll need to hunt down plainstriders (giant ostrich-looking things) until you get Tender Strider Meat, which you will then feed Kyle to get him to return home.

It's nice to see that while Blizzard has been pretty adamant about keeping the spirit of Classic World of Warcraft alive in Forever, it's willing to add a little wiggle room to add beloved pieces of WoW history like this quest. For as much as World of Warcraft has a reputation for gold selling and general toxicity, it's moments like this that remind me just how magical this game is, and how much it means to so many people.

item.title: System Shock 2 Remaster Is Free to Keep on the Epic Games Store Right Now
item.description: System Shock 2: 25th Anniversary Remaster is currently free to claim on the Epic Games Store until October 8, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
PC players can currently pick up System Shock 2: 25th Anniversary Remaster for free on the Epic Games Store until October 8, 2026. As with all of Epic's weekly freebies, anything you claim during the window stays in your library permanently. You'll need a free Epic Games account to claim System Shock 2, and the game is played through the Epic Games Launcher.

Nightdive Studios, the team behind a string of well-regarded classic revivals such as those for Quake and Star Wars: Dark Forces, released the 25th Anniversary Remaster in June 2025.

The update keeps the original design but modernises how it looks and plays, including the following changes:

  • Remastered visuals, including cutscenes, character models, and weapon models
  • Support for up to 4K at 144fps on PC
  • Adjustable field of view and ultrawide support
  • Full mod support
  • Cross-play co-op for up to four players
  • The choice of an O.S.A., Marine, or Navy background to shape your playstyle

The original System Shock 2 launched back in 1999, developed by Looking Glass Studios and Irrational Games, blending together an FPS shooter with the character building of an RPG. You wake from cryosleep aboard the faster-than-light ship Von Braun in the year 2114 with no memory of who you are, and the ship is overrun by hybrid mutants and hostile robots.

Its influence is hard to overstate. Many of the people behind it went on to make the BioShock games, which are often described as a spiritual successor to System Shock 2, and the game's blend of environmental storytelling and player choice has shaped plenty of what has followed. The original title garnered a 9/10 rating when it received an updated review. Now, this Epic Games Store deal offers a free way to revisit one of the most influential games ever made.

If the remaster whets your appetite, Nightdive also released a full remake of the first System Shock on PC in 2023, rebuilt with new HD visuals, updated controls and a revamped hacking system. It's a handy way to explore the series' roots, though System Shock 2 works perfectly well as a standalone adventure – that's currently $11.99 on Steam with a hefty 70% discount during the Autumn Sale.

Epic is also giving away Buried Stars this week, so it's worth heading to the store for both. It's an anime-style visual novel in which a group of contestants on a TV show must survive a mysterious attack. Like System Shock 2, it's available to claim until 8 October, and you can add both games to your library in a couple of clicks.

item.title: The Miami Heat Will Wear GTA 6-Themed Uniforms in a November Match Against Milwaukee
item.description: The Miami Heat is heading to Vice City for its next NBA match against the Milwaukee Bucks.
item.content:encoded:
The Miami Heat is heading to Vice City for its next NBA match against the Milwaukee Bucks. The one-night-only event, hosted live on ESPN, has been dubbed A Night in Vice City, and will see the home team donning an “all-new uniform on a never-before-seen court.”

Presumably, this means the team is sponsored by Take-Two and Rockstar Games for a GTA 6 marketing stunt. As they go, this is one of the cooler ones.

The event will take place at the Kaseya Center at 7pm EST/ 4pm PT on November 18, the day before GTA launches. A bunch of fancy crossover merch has also appeared on the Miami Heat store, celebrating Vice City.

Yesterday, the top of the Kaseya Center, home of The Heat, was lit up to usher in the collaboration between Rockstar and Miami’s home team. This followed a lengthy negotiation with local officials over the extent to which Rockstar could use Miami as a base for creative advertising.

GTA 6 takes place in Leonida, a fictional recreation of Florida housing its jewel, a virtual recreation of Miami called Vice City. In-game, the Kaseya Center is dubbed the Sahara Arena.

Other studios are taking notice of what Rockstar is doing in the lead-up to launch. Earlier, one of the founders of the studio behind Kingdom Come: Deliverance held up GTA 6’s pricing as a potential turning point for the industry and video game prices in general.

Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick previously commented on GTA 6’s price speculation, saying: “Consumers pay for the value that you bring to them, and our job is to charge way way way less of the value delivery.

GTA 6 costs $79.99 for the Standard Edition. The Ultimate Edition, which includes extra in-game content, costs $99.99. GTA 6 releases for PS5 and Xbox Series consoles on November 19.

item.title: Batman, Lord of the Rings, and Harry Potter Feature in First Trailer for Skydance, the Newly Named Parent Company for a Merged Warner Bros. and Paramount
item.description: Once merged, Harry Potter, Lord of the Rings and Game of Thrones company Warner Bros. will exist alongside Paramount as a sub-brand of Skydance.
item.content:encoded:
Once merged, Harry Potter, Lord of the Rings, and Game of Thrones company Warner Bros. will exist alongside Paramount as a sub-brand of Skydance.

The historic film and TV studios are being slapped together by David Ellison and backed by his billionaire dad Larry Ellison in a deal worth $110 billion, following a hostile bid for WB last year and despite various regulatory blocks that have attempted to scupper the deal in the U.S. and abroad. Concern has been raised that the merger may lead to thousands of job losses through corporate consolidation, afford control over a huge chunk of Hollywood to the Ellison family, and in turn risk the independence of news networks such as CNN.

However, opposition to the deal has now largely melted away and, with the merger's completion appearing imminent, Ellison has now confirmed that "Skydance" will be the name of his soon-to-be enormous entertainment empire. The Warner Bros. and Paramount branding will still be kept for their relevant subdivisions.

Indeed, a bombastic new trailer for Skydance has also been revealed, showcasing the vast swath of Warner Bros. and Paramount intellectual property that Skydance will have access to, including the DC Comics, Lord of the Rings, and Harry Potter franchises.

What once was the peak, is now just the beginning.

Paramount and Warner Bros. shaped over a century of culture. By combining them, we aren't rewriting history — we're equipping these iconic studios with a more powerful engine. Together, we are Skydance: a creative-first home for… pic.twitter.com/uInLRY3IrE

— David Ellison (@ellisonskydance) October 2, 2026

"These brands are more than a destination, they are the launch pad," a voiceover for the trailer states, in a script that sounds like it was written by an AI. "They don't just live on screens, they move through culture. Each one, distinct. Built on story. Driven by technology. A new center of gravity. A constellation. A shared vision to go beyond. Look up. What once was the peak, is now just the beginning."

Whatever that's supposed to mean, the trailer includes clips from notable WB and Paramount movies and TV series such as Inception, Titanic, Superman, Barbie, Minecraft, The Godfather, The Sopranos, Star Trek, The Matrix, Game of Thrones, The Shawshank Redemption, Casablanca, A Star is Born, Grease, Sinners, Forrest Gump, Dune, Ferris Bueller's Day Off, The Great Gatsby, and Euphoria.

A selection of brand logos shown at the end of the trailer highlights that Skydance will own Paramount, WB, DC Comics, CNN, Paramount+, CBS, Nickelodeon, and HBO Max, plus MTV, TCM, Showtime, Adult Swim, Comedy Central, Cartoon Network, Eurosport, Miramax, NewLine Cinema, Animal Planet, the UK's Channel 5, and many, many more.

The deal that will cement ownership of all this under Skydance is now expected to close on October 6, the companies have said.

item.title: 8 Big October Games We've Already Played if You Want to Know What We Think of Them So Far
item.description: October is here, which means the Fall is in full swing, which means some of the biggest games of the year drop this month. We've already played some of the biggest ones, so check out our previews of Phantom Blade Zero, Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, Final Fantasy Resonance, and more below.
item.content:encoded:
October is here, which means the Fall is in full swing, which means some of the biggest games of the year drop this month ahead of You Know Who. We've already played some of the biggest ones, so check out our previews of Phantom Blade Zero, Castlevania: Belmont's Curse, Final Fantasy Resonance, and more below.

Phantom Blade Zero

Release Date: October 29

There are three difficulty options to choose from, but even at the default setting that I played at, Phantom Blade Zero is hard, and I loved that about it. It never felt cheap; it just demanded more from me. In just over an hour of play, I was easily ten times the player I was when I started. It’s a feeling of achievement that is reserved for the very best action games on the planet. If the rest is anything like what I played, I feel like there’s a real chance that Phantom Blade 0 might be one of those games. Read our full Phantom Blade Zero preview.

Castlevania: Belmont's Curse

Release Date: October 15

I had an absolute blast with Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse. The art and animation are absolutely gorgeous; combat is fun and dynamic with plenty of room to carve out your own personal playstyle thanks to the variety of weapons, Arcana, and relics; exploration was appropriately rewarding and there were plenty of secrets hidden within the cracked walls of the Parisian streets; and the bosses provided a nice challenge without ever feeling too overwhelming for how early I was in the game. Read our full Castlevania: Belmont's Curse preview.

Final Fantasy Resonance

Release Date: October 22

Resonance has the most impressive use of HD-2D I think I’ve ever seen. It’s absolutely gorgeous, and you can see it from the overworld. It’s the way the clouds pass gently overhead, the way the wind seems to rustle the grass beneath your feet. What’s equally stunning is the way your character’s spite moves through all of this. HD-2D is gorgeous, but it can sometimes look like your character is a little out of place in the world. Not so here. Your character looks distinct, but it always seems like they fit. Read our full Final Fantasy Resonance preview.

Warhammer 40K: Boltgun 2

Release Date: October 14

Warhammer 40K was always such a natural pairing with what has come to be called the "boomer shooter" – these crunchy, nostalgic celebrations of ‘90s mayhem that take notes from the likes of old-school Doom, Quake, and Rise of the Triad. The original Boltgun was one of those team-ups that seems so obvious in retrospect that I was almost mad I didn't think of it myself. With Boltgun 2, the couple of levels I played show a desire to evolve a bit beyond those templates, though. It still has the look and feel of all the blood-drenched classics, while dialing up the scope and expanding the environments and character roster. Read our full Warhammer 40K: Boltgun 2 preview.

Emberville

Release Date: October 27

Between the mastery and class skill trees, loot, and stat points to distribute, Emberville already appeals to my love of ARPGs, while its gathering and crafting systems have the potential to appeal to a whole different crowd too, like my wife, who is a fan of cozier games. That could make Emberville one of those rare games that we can both enjoy together when it releases and serve as an introduction to the genres for both sides. Read our full Emberville preview.

Planet Zoo 2

Release Date: October 13

I didn't even start my Planet Zoo 2 career from the typical top-down strategy game perspective. Rather, I was placed directly into the world at ground height, allowing me to walk around the lush East African Rift Valley in first-person. While some previous Frontier games like Jurassic World Evolution have included this as a feature, making it the first thing you do before placing any buildings or fussing over graphs literally changed my perspective in a positive way. Read our full Planet Zoo 2 preview.

Nintendo Switch Sports Resort

Release Date: October 22

This series has not changed all that much in 20 years. Each sport used either a single Joy-Con or a split pair of them, relying almost entirely on simple motion controls with the occasional button press. I played 100-pin bowling, returning from the original Wii Sports Resort, where a lone red pin denotes the front of an army of pins to knock down. This was a classic back on the Wii, and I’m glad to see it back after it wasn’t included in 2022’s Nintendo Switch Sports. Read our full Nintendo Switch Spors Resort preview.

Stupid Never Dies

Release Date: October 22

While Stupid Never Dies isn’t necessarily a roguelike, it does have some of that DNA in its approach to progression. Each venture into the dungeon has a time limit, and Davy won’t be able to make it all the way to the KOM right away. You keep any loot you collect, but each fresh run resets Davy’s level back down to zero. However, as you progress further you will build an XP multiplier, allowing you to level up faster, and make it deeper on the next attempt. Read our full Stupid Never Dies preview.

item.title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance Dev Hopes GTA 6 Will Encourage Studios to Charge More for Their Games
item.description: Warhorse co-founder Martin Klima wants GTA 6 to “blaze a trail” for higher game prices.
item.content:encoded:
Warhorse co-founder Martin Klima wants GTA 6 to “blaze a trail” for higher game prices. Klima claimed triple-A games face an existential problem, with audience sizes plateauing, brick and mortar retail basically dead ("We destroyed retail, and we took all their money,” he said), and no new revenue streams to support the growing costs of making a big game.

Klima claimed that GTA 6 developer Rockstar and parent company Take-Two are in a unique position as the only companies "who can afford, or who can dare, to increase the price of games, which I think is long overdue and also necessary for this business to survive.

"The last thing you can do is to increase the unit price," Klima continued. "That would help a lot, but everybody's scared to death about it. Now, hopefully, GTA will blaze the trail, and it will allow us to increase the cost."

These comments come from an interview with PC Gamer, during which Klima admitted that GTA 6 “doesn't appeal to me at all” despite the series’ popularity. "I am not going to be playing GTA 6 unless I'm somehow forced to," he said. "And the reason why it is so popular — it beats me. It's something which I just fail to understand."

In the U.K., GTA 6 is priced £69.99 for the Standard Edition, which is pretty typical for a tentpole triple-A release. However, in the U.S. it’s $79.99 for the Standard Edition, 10 dollars higher than the usual price point of a new game. The Ultimate Edition, which includes in-game content most players will want, costs $99.99.

Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick previously commented on GTA 6’s price speculation, saying: “Consumers pay for the value that you bring to them, and our job is to charge way way way less of the value delivery. How you feel about something you buy is the intersection of the thing itself and what you pay for. Consumers need to feel like the thing itself is amazing and the price they were charged was fair for what they got.

“What we think about is making the most spectacular piece of entertainment on Earth, in history — and it’s a pretty daunting challenge. If we do that, and if we’re of service to our customers, then the upside will take care of itself.”

GTA 6 is widely speculated to be the most expensive game ever made, with Take-Two estimated to have spent between $1 billion to $2 billion developing and marketing the title. Yesterday, we wrote a story about a marketing stunt in Miami for GTA 6 that reportedly cost $1 million in itself.

The game is expected to be the most popular entertainment launch of all time, breaking records when it launches to the public this November. Analysts predict GTA 6 will generate $5.2 billion in sales by the end of launch week. GTA 6 releases for PS5 and Xbox Series consoles on November 19.

item.title: Original Xbox Version of Halo: Combat Evolved Made Available to Play in a Browser
item.description: The original Xbox version of Halo: Combat Evolved has been made available to play in a web browser.
item.content:encoded:
The original Xbox version of Halo: Combat Evolved has been made available to play in a web browser.

This is not a port of Bungie’s seminal 2001 first-person shooter, rather the original Xbox game running in your browser. Hot on the heels of decompilation work done elsewhere, AI developer Mitchell Hynes released Halo in a browser, hosting and maintaining the game himself.

Hynes made a point of explaining that this browser release is not Borderlands developer Gearbox's official and divisive 2003 PC port of Halo: Combat Evolved, no doubt to encourage veteran fans of the original to give it a shot. And his tweets appear to have gathered a great deal of attention. Five hours after releasing the game, it saw nearly 20,000 games, hitting an average of 94 frames per second.

Halo owner Microsoft may well take a dim view of the original Xbox Halo popping up in browsers, of course, despite the fact it’s free to play. Microsoft recently released Halo: Campaign Evolved on PC as well as consoles, and there can be no doubt that the company’s lawyers will see this browser version of the original as competition.

Indeed, some thought Microsoft had already taken action when Hynes’ website was flagged as “Suspected Phishing.” He insisted this was due to an automatic flag from Cloudflare, rather than Microsoft, and the ban was soon lifted.

We’re currently in the middle of an AI video game explosion that has seen various clips of famous games mashed together go viral as people use the likes of Claude to create “mods” much faster than previously possible. Some are using AI to create clones of famous games. Others are using AI to release versions of existing, traditionally made mods — much to their creators’ annoyance.

For video game publishers, the potential impact may be existential. Why buy a new Halo game if AI can spit one out for you in a matter of minutes? This week, the person behind a viral AI-generated Fallout: New York game pulled it offline after receiving a cease and desist from Bethesda, leading fans to celebrate. It will be interesting to see how long Halo in your browser stays online.

Meanwhile, Microsoft has handed the keys to the next mainline Halo game to Call of Duty company Activision, and gutted Halo Studios in the process.
